target_moa.text: Sotagliflozin is a dual inhibitor of SGLT2 and SGLT1; SGLT2 inhibition reduces renal reabsorption of glucose and sodium, while SGLT1 inhibition reduces intestinal absorption of glucose and sodium

citations.quote: Sotagliflozin is an inhibitor of SGLT2 and SGLT1. Inhibiting SGLT2 reduces renal reabsorption of glucose and sodium which may influence several physiological functions such as lowering both pre-and afterload of the heart and downregulating sympathetic activity. Inhibiting SGLT1 reduces intestinal absorption of glucose and sodium which likely contributes to diarrhea. The mechanism for sotagliflozin

Sotagliflozin is an NME purported to be a dual SGLT1 and SGLT2 inhibitor. SGLT1 inhibition in the intestine results in delayed intestinal glucose absorption and stimulates gastrointestinal peptides. SGLT2 inhibition results in decreased glucose reabsorption in the renal proximal tubules and increased urinary glucose excretion and osmotic diuresis.

summary.text: NDA 216203 was submitted 5/27/2022 as a standard-review NDA under section 505(b) and approved on a first cycle based on two phase 3 trials (SOLOIST and SCORED); it was the first market approval for sotagliflozin, though a prior Complete Response (22 March 2019) had been issued under separate NDA 210934 for a glycemic control indication. No accelerated approval, breakthrough, fast track, or orphan designation applied, and no REMS or advisory committee meeting was required.
